Roblox claims to have made changes to its hugely popular children's app to protect kids from predators, but regulators say the protections are insufficient.

The regulator found four major shortfalls, including that adults can send friend requests to children without parental approval…

Australia's eSafety Commissioner has published the flaws it found during testing:

  • adults can send friend requests to young Australian children without parental or guardian consent;
  • children and adults can view and respond to each other's posts in off-platform forums without parental or guardian consent;
  • children's friend lists are visible to anyone on Roblox;
  • children's profiles and bios — including account name, number of friends and their names, avatar images, and non-sensitive personal data such as their interests — are publicly accessible to anyone on Roblox, with no ability to restrict visibility of this information.

The regulator says Roblox has agreed to implement stronger measures within three months:

  • preventing adults from contacting unknown children without parental consent
  • strengthening children's account settings so they default to private
  • setting up a usable reporting mechanism and notifying users of complaint outcomes
  • engaging an independent third-party auditor to assess the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of its age-estimation measures

Roblox has more than 380 million active users, the majority of whom are under the age of 16.
